content.title: About
content.content: Fruit smoothie is a beverage made from whole fruits without any dairy ingredients. It retains most of the fiber, vitamins, and minerals found in fresh fruit and is suitable for those avoiding dairy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Smoothies made with whole fruit retain more fiber than juice made from the same amount of fruit.
The absence of dairy makes it suitable for vegans and people with lactose intolerance.
A wide variety of fruits allows easy flavor changes and nutritional tweaks.
Combining different fruits can provide a broader spectrum of antioxidants than a single‑fruit blend.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: Fruit smoothies provide vitamin C, vitamin A, folate, and other micronutrients that support immunity and skin health.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Whole fruits keep dietary fiber intact, aiding digestion and promoting satiety.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Without dairy, the drink is low‑calorie and contains minimal saturated fat.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids from the fruit help combat free radicals and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high water content of fresh fruit contributes to overall fluid balance.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even though natural, fruit smoothies can be high in fructose, which should be considered by people with diabetes or those monitoring weight.

items.title: Allergies
items.content: Certain fruits (e.g., kiwi, mango) may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Microbial growth
items.content: If left at room temperature for more than 2 hours, the smoothie can become a breeding ground for bacteria. Consume immediately or refrigerate.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the smoothie on its own, use it as a base for breakfast bowls, add to oatmeal, plant‑based yogurt, or incorporate into dessert recipes. Optional add‑ins include chia seeds, nuts, or protein powder.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared smoothie in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized containers.
